title: Exploring the impact of artificial intelligence on dental education: Benefits, challenges, and future directions – A systematic review of the literature
text_snippet: Exploring the impact of artificial intelligence on dental education: Benefits, challenges, and future directions – A systematic review of the literature The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) in dental education is a profound opportunity, spurred on by unprecedented technological change. It should be revamped in a way that supports immense capabilities, improves efficiency, and provides learning opportunities, but also has constraints that need to be understood. Thus, in this article, we discuss the benefits and challenges involved in adapting AI into dental education, as well as methods to improve the application of AI to enhance learning for students and instructors. We reviewed a total of 73 articles from multiple databases, including PubMed/Medline, Cochrane, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Through our review of articles from the past five years (2018–2024), the selected studies were evaluated based on relevance, recency, and credibility, which were sometimes difficult to distinguish between. We ultimately found 56 articles that met the above criteria for relevance. title: Spiritual well-being, sleep quality as a buffer against burnout and in increasing professional fulfillment among healthcare professionals in the United Arab Emirates
text_snippet: Spiritual well-being, sleep quality as a buffer against burnout and in increasing professional fulfillment among healthcare professionals in the United Arab Emirates BACKGROUND: Burnout is a growing concern among healthcare professionals (HCPs) in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Emerging evidence suggests that sleep quality and spiritual well-being may buffer against burnout and enhance professional fulfilment. This study explores the relationship between sleep disturbance, spiritual well-being, and burnout among HCPs in the UAE. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 661 healthcare professionals across the UAE. Validated instruments were used to measure sleep quality, circadian regularity, spiritual well-being, burnout, and professional fulfilment. text_snippet: The impact of helicopter teaching in nursing education and approaches to foster independent learning: A narrative review The ‘helicopter teaching’ in nursing education can be harmful to the development of clinical judgement, decision-making, and autonomy among nursing students because it involves excessive control, constant supervision, and over-dependence. This narrative review examines the impact of helicopter teaching on the academic and professional development of nursing students. It also discusses evidence-based approaches that encourage independent learning and resilience. We searched databases such as PubMed, CINAHL, and Scopus with a mixture of search terms and Medical Subject Headings to analyze the evidence between 2010 and 2024. The review identified several contributing factors behind this helicopter style of teaching including faculty anxiety, a lack of confidence in student competency, and institutional pressures relating to patient safety. text_snippet: A neuroeducational approach to STEM education: Integrating real-time cognitive analysis and cognitive load theory to optimize teaching and learning at universities BACKGROUND: The relevance of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education to effectively meet challenging academic requirements has become imperative for university entrants. With emerging advancements within the domain of learning neuroscience and analytics, it has become possible to analyze and track the real-time mental states of learners. This has opened several avenues to apply the theoretical perspectives of Cognitive Load Theory (CLT). Though applications of neuro-technological interventions for learning have become widely sought, their effective implementation within STEM education has not been comprehensive at the university level. The innovations brought about within this study include its conceptual fusion for STEM education based upon real-time mental state analysis and CLT. The goal of this research is to integrate the current research findings on real-time cognitive analysis practices used in STEM education in universities and analyze how cognitive load can be monitored dynamically and discuss teaching practices according to principles of CLT to improve effectiveness and inclusiveness for better cognitive load management throughout learning. text_snippet: Global perspectives on health tourism: A comparative review of research trends and future prospects (2000–2024) This study systematically reviews global research trends in health tourism (2000–2024), comparing international and Chinese scholarly perspectives to identify key themes, differences, and future directions for the field. We employed a systematic literature analysis approach, examining studies on health tourism definitions, classifications, motivations, influencing factors, evaluation systems, and development strategies. Comparative insights were drawn between international and Chinese research priorities. Findings reveal distinct research emphases: International scholars focus on global perspectives, interdisciplinary integration, cross-border service delivery, and ethical concerns, while Chinese researchers prioritize localized frameworks, regional characteristics, and policy applications. Both groups, however, share an interest in industrial integration and growth drivers. text_snippet: Transforming lupus self-care education with mobile health: A systematic review Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic, multisystemic, autoimmune, and inflammatory disease with complex and variable phenotypes and clinical presentations. text_snippet: Impact of music therapy on diabetes distress and bio-physiological parameters in patients with diabetic foot ulcer BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a common and significant complication of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus (DM), frequently resulting in increased physiological suffering and emotional burden. Music therapy, as a complementary intervention, has shown potential in lowering stress and improving general well-being, but its influence on patients with DFU is unknown. text_snippet: Managing public education on smoking behavior in families with stunted children: Between challenges and opportunities in Indonesia BACKGROUND: Stunting remains a major public health concern in Indonesia, compounded by the country’s high prevalence of smoking. This study explores the smoking behavior of families with stunted children, parental knowledge of smoking-related risks, and their motivation for behavioral change. title: Identifying the requirements for the implementation of teledentistry in rural areas: A scoping review protocol
text_snippet: Identifying the requirements for the implementation of teledentistry in rural areas: A scoping review protocol Oral health disparities in rural areas of developing countries are exacerbated by geographic barriers, limited infrastructure, and workforce shortages. Teledentistry, a branch of telemedicine, offers a promising solution to improve access to dental care. This scoping review aims to identify the infrastructure, workforce, and patient-related requirements for implementing teledentistry in rural settings. In this scoping review, Arksey and O’Malley’s five-stage framework will be used. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase databases will be used to search for studies using a detailed search strategy. title: “ALIADA” educational nutrition intervention for adolescents: Content and preliminary face validity
text_snippet: “ALIADA” educational nutrition intervention for adolescents: Content and preliminary face validity BACKGROUND: Educational nutrition interventions include diverse learning experiences aimed at improving specific populations’ eating behaviors. To ensure the success of these interventions, a thorough formative evaluation, careful planning of objectives and activities, and rigorous validation of the intervention are essential. In this study, the face and content validity of “ALIADA”, an educational nutrition intervention for adolescents based on the Social Cognitive Theory (SCT), was carried out. To our knowledge, this is the first validated intervention program based on the SCT for Mexican adolescents in the late stage. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The content validity was evaluated by 13 experts, including relevance, effectiveness, and appropriateness of each intervention activity. After modifications were made to the activities, five experts evaluated the revised version of the intervention. The Content Validity Index for each Item (I-CVI) and the Content Validity Index for the entire Series of Items (S-CVI) were used. title: The role of health literacy in the prevalence of cardiovascular diseases: A systematic review
text_snippet: The role of health literacy in the prevalence of cardiovascular diseases: A systematic review Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a major public health challenge, and health literacy (HL) is a key tool in health promotion that can improve outcomes in both patients and healthy populations. While the relationship between HL and secondary and tertiary prevention of CVD has been studied, its role in primary prevention has received less attention. This systematic review aimed to examine and synthesize the existing literature on the relationship between HL and CVD prevalence. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines between September and December 2023 in the scientific databases PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus. The search had a 15-year timeframe and used specific keywords. Included studies were freely available in full-text, published in English and focused on healthy adults or populations without diagnosed CVDs. METHODS AND MATERIAL: This semi-experimental study was conducted on 135 children admitted to Ali Ibn Abitaleb Hospital in Rafsanjan. The children were randomly divided into three groups. title: Emotional regulation skills among deaf students: Challenges and effective interventions
text_snippet: Emotional regulation skills among deaf students: Challenges and effective interventions BACKGROUND: This study examines affective regulation among hearing-impaired learners, emphasizing the challenges they face and strategies to enhance emotional management. Emotional regulation is vital for academic and social success, particularly in inclusive settings where communication barriers elevate stress. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A bibliometric analysis was conducted on academic publications retrieved from the Scopus database for the period 2012–2024. Keywords related to hearing impairment, emotional regulation, social development, and educational interventions were applied. The study analyzed publication trends, research hotspots, and thematic clusters to identify key directions in the field. RESULTS: Research output on this topic has grown substantially over the past decade. Major themes include early intervention programs, the development of social competence, and the role of parental support in fostering emotional stability. Frequently studied strategies involve emotional intelligence training, inclusive classroom practices, and teacher preparedness. title: Ubiquinol supplementation in cardiovascular diseases: A systematic review of clinical efficacy and therapeutic potential
text_snippet: Ubiquinol supplementation in cardiovascular diseases: A systematic review of clinical efficacy and therapeutic potential Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a leading global cause of morbidity and mortality, with oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction playing key roles in their progression. Though conventional therapies exist, interest in adjunct treatments such as ubiquinol—a bioactive form of coenzyme Q10 with superior bioavailability—has grown due to its potential to improve cardiac function and reduce oxidative damage. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy of ubiquinol in managing CVDs, with a focus on its comparative benefits over ubiquinone. The review followed the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta‐analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, analysing randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from various databases. Databases including Cochrane (1,441 records), PubMed (1,178), Web of Science (252), and Scopus (1,514) were searched, identifying 4,385 records. text_snippet: Effect of a peer-facilitated education program on disease knowledge among adolescents with sickle cell disease: A randomized controlled trial in Kenya BACKGROUND: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, characterized by chronic anemia, recurrent vaso-occlusive crises, and significant morbidity. Adolescents and young adults increasingly assume responsibility for disease self-management; however, limited disease knowledge may hinder effective self-care and contribute to preventable complications. This study evaluated the effect of a structured youth support group education program on disease knowledge among adolescents and young adults living with SCD in Kenya. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A two-arm parallel randomized controlled trial was conducted among 104 adolescents and young adults aged between 13 and 24 years with confirmed SCD attending outpatient follow-up in Nairobi County, Kenya. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to a peer-facilitated youth support group education program ( n = 52) or routine clinical care ( n = 52).
